newsitem.title: USA: Actor Brian Keith apparently kills himself in Malibu.
newsitem.headline: Actor Brian Keith apparently kills himself in Malibu.

text.p: Actor Brian Keith, best known as a bachelor raising three orphans in the TV series "Family Affair," apparently committed suicide on Tuesday, a sheriff's department spokesman said.
Sgt. Noel Lanier said Keith, 75, was found dead in his home in the movie star colony of Malibu, overlooking the Pacific Ocean.
The officer said detectives were at the scene. The exact cause of death had not been determined, but suicide was suspected.
There was no immediate comment from Keith's representative, Bob Schiller, at Guild Management.
"Sheriff's homicide detectives are investigating the apparent suicide of actor Brian Keith," said Lanier, who referred all further calls to Guild Management.

Keith was born in Bayonne, New Jersey, on Nov. 14, 1921. After serving in the U.S. Marines in the Second World War, he went into stock theatre and radio and also appeared on Broadway in "Mr. Roberts" and "Darkness at Noon".
On film, the burly actor was in "The Parent Trap," "Nevada Smith" and a host of other movies, including several Disney films.

He also starred in a number of short-lived TV series, including "The Westerner" (1960), "Archer" (1975), "Hardcastle & McCormick" (1983-1986), "Pursuit of Happiness (1987-1988) and "Heartland" (1989).
But he was best known for "Family Affair", which ran from 1966-71. He played Bill Davis, a swinging Manhattan bachelor with an English butler, Mr. French, played by Sebastian Cabot.
His life was turned upside down when he was called on to raise his brother's three children -- twins Buffy and Jody, and 15-year-old Cissy.
The actress who played Buffy on the programme, Anissa Jones, later died of a drug overdose.

Keith also brought his trademark low-key humour and easygoing style to his role as pediatrician Dr. Sean Jamison on the series "The Brian Keith Show." The show, titled "The Little People" during its first season, ran on NBC from the fall of 1972 through August of 1974.
In recent years, Keith had been doing "voice-over" work on TV commercials.
